one_liner: C++ RTP/SRTP/ZRTP library with built-in H.264/HEVC/VVC packetization; its authors report 4.4x FFmpeg's RTP goodput.
what_it_does: Sends and receives RTP media streams: a uvgrtp::context creates sessions (one per peer address), each session creates media_streams, and push_frame(buffer, len, flags) packetizes a whole encoded frame (start-code lookup, fragmentation units, aggregation packets) for AVC/HEVC/VVC/V3C, while Opus and RFC 3551 audio formats go out unfragmented. The receiver gets frames through pull_frame() or a callback installed with install_receive_hook() and frees each one with uvgrtp::frame::dealloc_frame(). SRTP is keyed by ZRTP or by the application (Crypto++ is optional), and RTCP is opt-in. It is transport only: no RTSP/SDP signalling, containers or codecs, so it is not a drop-in replacement for libavformat or Live555.
how_it_is_fast: The NAL start-code lookup scans 8 bytes at a time with the SWAR 'has a zero byte' bit trick (haszero64/haszero32) instead of testing byte by byte. On the send side, RTP and FU headers sit in small separate buffers and are gathered with the caller's payload through iovecs into sendmmsg(2) (WSASendTo on Windows), so frame data is not copied unless RTP_COPY is set; RCE_SYSTEM_CALL_CLUSTERING batches up to 1024 packets per sendmmsg call. On the receive side a dedicated receiver thread (it requests SCHED_FIFO priority on Linux) fills a preallocated ring buffer and a separate processor thread reassembles fragments into frames allocated with the start code already in place. Each NAL unit reaches the callback as soon as it is complete, with no access-unit parser holding it back.
when_to_use: Streaming pre-encoded H.264, HEVC or VVC (or V3C atlas) bitstreams between endpoints you control, with your own signalling.
4K/8K or high-frame-rate video over a 10 GbE LAN, where per-packet CPU cost and kernel buffering limit the frame rate (larger socket buffers and RCE_PACE_FRAGMENT_SENDING are documented for bursts).
Low-latency links where the receiver should get each NAL unit through a callback without demuxer or parser buffering.
Encrypted point-to-point media (SRTP with ZRTP or user-managed keys) without pulling in a WebRTC stack.
C++17 projects on Linux or Windows that need a BSD-2-Clause RTP stack, with an ABI-stable C-style Core API in shared builds.
when_not_to_use: You need RTSP/SDP signalling, container demuxing or decoding: FFmpeg, Live555 or GStreamer cover the whole pipeline, and uvgRTP covers only the RTP transport.
WebRTC interop (ICE, DTLS-SRTP, congestion control): not provided. RTCP report blocks are exposed, but congestion control is left to the application.

Strict RFC interop with third-party receivers: open issues report that the H26x marker bit is set per NAL unit rather than per access unit (#261) and that the RTP timestamp is incremented incorrectly by default (#246); the 4.0.0 release notes list both as known issues.
Heavy RTCP use: open issues report a crash in rtcp::update_session_statistics (#235, labelled critical) and a segfault during RTCP teardown (#262).

macOS (community-supported only), 32-bit targets (a 64-bit compiler is required), or access units that hold several large NAL units needing fragmentation (the docs warn this may lead to undefined behaviour).

integration.form: static lib (default; full Extended C++ API) or shared lib (UVGRTP_BUILD_SHARED, Core API only)
integration.dependencies: pthreads; Crypto++ optional (auto-detected with __has_include) for SRTP/ZRTP
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17), CMake 3.14+, 64-bit GCC, MinGW or MSVC
integration.platforms: Linux and Windows (x86-64 builds documented); macOS community-supported
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each reception flow runs its own receiver and processor threads, and receive hooks are called on library threads

gotchas: push_frame() runs start-code lookup by default. Pass RTP_NO_H26X_SCL if your encoder hands over bare NAL units. The receiver prepends start codes unless RCE_H26X_DO_NOT_PREPEND_SC is set, and frames arrive per NAL unit, not per access unit.

push_frame() does not take ownership and works in place: SRTP in-place encryption is the default, so the caller's buffer is modified unless RTP_COPY is passed. Every received frame must be released with uvgrtp::frame::dealloc_frame().

Defaults are 4 MB socket and ring buffers. For bursty 4K60+ traffic the docs suggest 40-80 MB buffers and fragment pacing (RCE_PACE_FRAGMENT_SENDING, which sleeps inside push_frame), and the benchmark harness itself sets 40 MB. sendmmsg clustering is opt-in and the docs warn it can raise frame loss at high frame rates.
Use 4.0.1 or later: that release adds protection against out-of-bounds memory access on invalid headers (extension header length checks), and 4.0.0 added checks for too-small payloads.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The only transport sibling is rustrtc (a Rust WebRTC stack measured against webrtc-rs and pion). Pick uvgRTP for plain RTP/SRTP in C++ with native HEVC/VVC/AVC packetization and no ICE/DTLS, and rustrtc when browsers must connect. Codec siblings such as Kvazaar (same group; the benchmark files are Kvazaar-encoded), dav1d or VVenC are complementary: uvgRTP carries their output.
verified_claims_summary: The only numbers are from the uvgRTP authors' MMSP 2020 abstract, seen as a search snippet: sending a Kvazaar-encoded 4K HEVC file from a Core i7-4770 over 10 GbE, uvgRTP reached 5.0 Gb/s, 4.4x FFmpeg libavformat's peak goodput with 92.1% lower round-trip latency, and over 2x Live555's goodput with 82.3% lower latency. The rtp-benchmarks harness (g++ -O2 -g) is public but has no result files, and the library versions and build flags are not stated. Reading that harness shows that FFmpeg's latency path was measured with its default HEVC parser buffering and with the intended low-latency options silently unset (see measurement_notes), so the latency gap mostly reflects configuration, not RTP stack speed.
status_note: Actively maintained (Release 4.0.1 on 2026-07-28, after the ABI-safe 4.0.0 in May 2026) and BSD-2-Clause, so it is copyable. The benchmark repository's last commit is 2024-01-23, and its README says the FFmpeg and Live555 harnesses may no longer work out of the box.
measurement_notes: Harness findings for the orchestrator (ultravideo/rtp-benchmarks, both the initial commit 7151dba of 2020-06-10, which predates the MMSP 2020 paper, and HEAD). (1) Latency, FFmpeg side. Both versions call av_dict_set(&d_r, "nobuffer", NULL, 32) and av_dict_set(&d_s, "flush_packets", NULL, 32). In the FFmpeg API a NULL value deletes the key, so these low-latency options were never applied, and 'nobuffer' is an fflags value, not an option name. FFmpeg's HEVC RTP depacketizer declares need_parsing = AVSTREAM_PARSE_FULL (libavformat/rtpdec_hevc.c), so av_read_frame runs the HEVC parser, which closes a frame only when it sees the next access unit's first NAL (hevc_find_frame_end). At the harness's hard-coded 30 fps that can hold each frame about one 33 ms frame interval on each of the two FFmpeg receive hops (echo side and measuring side). uvgRTP's hook fires per NAL unit immediately. The 92.1% lower latency is therefore largely a configuration artifact, not RTP-stack speed. (2) Also in the FFmpeg latency sender: send times sit in a std::deque that the receiver thread pops one per received AVPacket (FIFO), and the code's own comment says start-code lookup and merging of small packets change packet boundaries. parse.pl expects 598 FFmpeg packets against 602 for uvgRTP and 601 for Live555, so any merge shifts every later FFmpeg latency by whole frame periods. The deque and an unordered_map are shared between the two threads with no lock (data race). A chunk whose size is already in the map is skipped with 'continue' before the offset advances; in 2020 this desynchronised the inline size-prefixed file walk, and at HEAD it sends the following chunks from the wrong offset. (3) Both libraries' latencies are floored to whole milliseconds per frame (diff / 1000 on integer microseconds) before averaging, which favours whichever stack has lower latency. (4) The 2020 uvgRTP sender used RCE_SYSTEM_CALL_DISPATCHER, a send-thread mode that current uvgRTP lists as removed, so the measured configuration no longer exists. (5) HEAD-only regressions, not behind the 2020 numbers: the uvgRTP goodput receiver uses tid = thread_num / 2 while main() now passes thread_num = i, so threads 0 and 1 share one counter slot in multi-stream runs. EXPECTED_FRAMES is 604 in uvgrtp_util.hh against TOTAL_FRAMES_UVGRTP = 602 in parse.pl. The SRTP setup loop writes the salt values into key[] and leaves the salt zero. The FFmpeg goodput receiver's interrupt callback aborts after 10 ms without a packet (its comment says 300 ms) against uvgRTP's 200 ms. Tier C stands. The goodput claim cannot be checked (no results), and the latency claim should carry this caveat.
